issues.why: Omits the critical lid-removal step. Dutch oven recipes universally require removing the lid after ~20 min to allow the crust to brown and crisp. A user following only this atom would leave the lid on the entire bake and get a pale, steamed, non-crispy crust.

States crust ranges from thin and crispy to thick and chewy, but thick crusts from longer/hotter baking are crispier, not chewier. Thick and chewy is a property of soft-crumb breads, not thick-crusted ones. A user would be misled about what to expect from their crust.

Framing rise as the PURPOSE of CO2 production misleads users. The biological purpose of fermentation is microbial energy metabolism; the CO2 and acids are byproducts. Users may misunderstand why fermentation timing and yeast activity matter for structure.

Claims aroma compounds are trapped within the crumb during baking and cooling. In fact, most fermentation volatiles evaporate at baking temperatures. What remains as aroma comes from Maillard reaction and caramelization products formed during baking, not trapped fermentation compounds.

Describes trapping steam but omits when to release it. Without knowing the lid comes off partway through (after ~20 min), a user would leave it sealed the entire bake and not achieve the crust development the dutch oven technique is meant to produce.
